lines.text: Dutch people make many appointments [afspraken], with formal contacts [formele contacten]: the family doctor, the dentist, the physiotherapist [fysiotherapeut], the hospital, an official body/agency [instantie] such as the municipality, a job interview [sollicitatiegesprek], at work, or at your child's school.
Also for informal contacts [informele contacten] — visits to family or friends — Dutch people usually make an appointment.
For informal appointments most people message each other on WhatsApp [appen].
A formal appointment can sometimes be made via a website or by email, but usually you have to make the appointment by phone [telefonisch].
You must be able to explain [uitleggen] with whom and why you want an appointment.
You must be able to spell your surname [achternaam kunnen spellen].
Sometimes you have to give more information, for example your date of birth [geboortedatum] or your address.
You must write down [noteren] when, where and with whom the appointment is.
For formal appointments it is important to arrive on time [op tijd].
If you cannot make it on time, you must call or send a short message [berichtje].
If you have to cancel [afzeggen] the appointment, call in time — usually 24 hours [24 uur] before the appointment.
If you don't show up and didn't call in time (for example at the dentist)?
Then you may still receive a bill [rekening].
If you forgot an appointment, you should also give them a call.
